subject: Hosted API discount tiers — metric appendix & rounding approach
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@quantafin.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Kyle Evans <kyle.evans@quantafin.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Draft pricing structure — clarifying how billed units map to sessions

Hi Olga / Laura,

Thanks again for the call this morning — we like Redwood's latency profile and the routing controls. Before we move to a commercial draft, procurement asked for a very specific explanation of how "billable units" will be measured for our streaming-heavy workload. Two short asks: 

1) If a single user opens a streaming completion that sends/receives partial tokens over several minutes, how is that accounted for against the monthly commit? Does each partial flush round up to the nearest token, or do you aggregate per-session? We want to avoid a surprise where every single flush is rounded up, multiplying billable units.

2) For the volume discount slabs in your initial quote, are those calculated on raw billable units per calendar month or on a rolling 30-day sum? Also, are overage bill rates prorated or bumped to the next slab threshold?

We'd appreciate a short appendix or example calculations (a few rows with realistic numbers) so our finance team can map this to forecasted spend.

Attachments: none

Best,
Maya Singh
Director, Procurement
QuantaFin

From: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@quantafin.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft pricing structure — clarifying how billed units map to sessions

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, and I attached a one-page pricing appendix with worked examples.

1) Streaming sessions: Redwood measures billable units as "consumable tokens" emitted by the model. For streaming, we aggregate by session (session = single API stream established by the caller) and meter on the session-level sum before applying rounding. That means intermittent flushes inside a session are accumulated and rounded once at the end of the session window, not per flush.

2) Discount slabs: Slabs are calculated on billable units consumed within the invoice period. For hosted customers on monthly invoices that's calendar-month aggregation by default; we can agree to a rolling 30-day window in enterprise contracts if needed. Overage is billed at the slab rate that covers the final billable unit bucket for the invoice period (no retroactive recomputation of earlier slabs).

I'll let Rishi add a short note below about edge cases (e.g., multi-tenant multiplexing, long-idle sessions).

Attachment: Redwood_PRICING_APPENDIX.xlsx (contains per-session examples, rounding rules, sample slab math)

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@quantafin.com>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft pricing structure — clarifying how billed units map to sessions

Maya — a couple of technical notes to make the appendix actionable for your engineering and finance teams.

- Aggregation window: session-level aggregation works in most cases. For designs where clients open many short-lived streams with identical session ids (e.g., multiplexed websockets), we recommend using a request-side session identifier to ensure correct aggregation. If clients use multiple connections without a persistent session id, each connection is treated as a discrete session for rounding purposes.

- Idle time cutoff: we close a session for billing if no tokens are emitted for 20 minutes by default; that cutoff is configurable in enterprise SOWs. 

- Rounding rule: we round billable units to the nearest whole token after summing the session total. We do not use sub-token billing. Example: session emits 102.7 tokens (sum of partial flushes) -> billed as 103 tokens. If a customer needs percentile-based smoothing for monthly invoicing for internal chargeback, we can export both raw unrounded counts and final billed counts in the invoice CSV.

- Streaming attachments: if a stream triggers multiple model calls (e.g., tool calls inside a session), those are still aggregated into the session total before rounding.

Happy to run this by your infra team if you want a short tech-to-tech call.

-Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Draft pricing structure — clarifying how billed units map to sessions

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple quick follow-ups from our finance/ops side: 

- Can you confirm whether tokens used for internal system prompts (e.g., safety classifiers we route) are billed to our account or if Redwood excludes model-side monitoring tokens from billable units?

- For slab calculation: if our month ends at 11:59pm PST but some tokens are ingested at 00:05 UTC, will that appear on the same invoice month? We have some users across timezones and want to avoid double-reporting in forecasts.

We may accept the calendar-month default but want to ensure the invoices match the stated aggregation.

Thanks,
Kyle
Sr. Cloud Architect
QuantaFin

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@quantafin.com>, Kyle Evans <kyle.evans@quantafin.com>
Cc: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft pricing structure — clarifying how billed units map to sessions

Hi Maya / Kyle — looping in Karthik (pricing) to confirm contract language. Per our discussion and Rishi's note, here are the proposed clauses we plan to include in the SOW and pricing appendix. I've attached a redline of the SOW (SOW-draft-v3.docx) with the same language.

1) Definitions (billing): "Billable Token" means a single whole token as emitted by the model runtime. For streaming endpoints, billable tokens are calculated by summing all tokens emitted during a session and rounding to the nearest whole token for billing. Sub-token fractions are not charged.

2) Invoice period & slabs: Volume discounts will be applied to billable tokens consumed within the invoice period. The Parties agree that the invoice period default is a calendar month in the customer's billing timezone (Customer Timezone = PST for QuantaFin). Upon request, Parties may elect a rolling 30-day aggregation in writing for an enterprise billing arrangement. Overage on an invoice will be charged using the slab rate that corresponds to the invoice-period total (i.e., slab pricing is not retroactively recomputed across prior invoices).

3) Monitoring & safety calls: Tokens consumed by Redwood-internal telemetry and safety classifiers operating on customer streams will not be charged to Customer. Tokens emitted by the model as part of customer-request handling (including model tool calls invoked by customer prompts) will be counted as billable. Redwood will provide CSV export with both raw unrounded token counts and the final billed token counts for reconciliation.

4) Session termination: Session aggregation uses the session identifier provided by the client. If no session identifier is supplied, Redwood will default to connection-level aggregation. Sessions with no emitted tokens for 20 consecutive minutes will be considered terminated for billing purposes.

If that aligns with your procurement needs we'll mark this as the pricing appendix and proceed to the final SOW/DocuSign. If you'd prefer a rolling window, let me know and we can capture an addendum that switches aggregation semantics (this is mostly an accounting preference; the underlying telemetry we export stays the same).

Attachment: SOW-draft-v3.docx (redline includes the clauses above)

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference
